contents.name: Finite sector structure and entropy convention

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-dimensional sector representation and matrix-state setup in Appendix A.7.2-A.7.3.
source_review.supports: Provides contextual finite-state entropy conventions for the local count model.
source_review.limitations: Harlow does not prove the arbitrary nonnegative-matrix path count; that is proved locally. No universal area law or gravitational interpretation is imported.

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-sector entropy decomposition and its stated hypotheses.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent finite-dimensional treatment of the entropy convention used by the local proposition.
source_review.limitations: The vector recursion, special matrix calculation, and path orientation are proved locally; no holographic conclusion is used.

sources.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, complete author-hosted book manuscript
sources.locator: Complete 598-page book manuscript; Section 5.2.1-5.2.2, PDF pp. 266-269, including Propositions 5.20-5.21 and Eqs. (5.94)-(5.99).
sources.reading_extent: The complete book manuscript was retrieved and the finite-dimensional entropy sections were inspected in batch 125. The current item convention uses natural logarithms and nats; Watrous’s displayed convention is base two.

source_review.read_extent: Read the definitions and finite spectral entropy discussion in Section 5.2.
source_review.supports: Supplies an independent textbook treatment of finite-dimensional density matrices and entropy.
source_review.limitations: Watrous uses base-two logarithms; the local entropy supplier explicitly uses natural logarithms and nats.

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite entropy and maximally mixed state formulas in Section 5.2.
source_review.supports: Independently covers the matrix entropy formula used in the local proof.
source_review.limitations: The local finite graph model and path recursion are proved without importing quantum-information results.

source_review.read_extent: Read the book’s finite-dimensional entropy conventions and examples.
source_review.supports: Supports the finite spectral entropy convention used with the local projection.
source_review.limitations: The Temperley-Lieb idempotence and representation hypotheses are not sourced from Watrous.

sources.title: Joshua Chen, The Temperley-Lieb Categories and Skein Modules, complete thesis
sources.locator: Complete 74-page thesis; Section 2.3, Theorem 2.3.2 and Proposition 2.3.6, PDF pp. 20-24 (printed pp. 11-15).
sources.reading_extent: The complete thesis PDF and extracted text were available locally; the full relevant Section 2.3 reasoning was read, including the recursive construction, uniqueness, annihilation/idempotence proof, reflection property, and closure trace.

source_review.read_extent: Read Definition 2.3.1 and the complete proof of Theorem 2.3.2, including the unit-denominator use and induction.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent diagrammatic treatment of the Jones-Wenzl recursion and projector properties.
source_review.limitations: Chen works over a generic field/category and proves diagrammatic statements, not the finite Hilbert representation or its self-adjoint image entropy.

source_review.read_extent: Read Theorem 2.3.2 and Proposition 2.3.6, including the horizontal reflection and closure-trace arguments.
source_review.supports: Independently corroborates the exact algebraic projector properties used from the pinned supplier.
source_review.limitations: The local proof separately establishes self-adjointness after a specified finite-dimensional representation; no area or boundary physics is inferred.

sources.title: Zhenghan Wang, Topological Quantum Computation, CBMS Regional Conference Series in Mathematics 112, complete book
sources.locator: Complete 129-page book; Chapter 1, Section 1.1.4, Theorem 1.12 and displayed recursive construction, PDF pp. 18-20 (book pp. 5-7).
sources.reading_extent: The complete book PDF was retrieved. Section 1.1.4 was inspected for its generic Temperley-Lieb loop convention, projector characterization, recursion, uniqueness, and closure trace. The text sketches some inductive verifications, so no omitted detail is treated as a supplied proof.

source_review.read_extent: Read the generic diagram-algebra setup and Theorem 1.12, including the recursion and generic denominator condition.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent book treatment and diagrammatic notation for Jones-Wenzl projectors.
source_review.limitations: The book uses its Kauffman loop variable and Chebyshev polynomials; no parameter substitution is assumed without the local recurrence definition.

source_review.read_extent: Read Theorem 1.12 and the trace recurrence on PDF pp. 18-20.
source_review.supports: Provides independent context for the algebraic idempotent and closure scalar.
source_review.limitations: Some annihilation checks are stated as straightforward; the local argument relies on the complete pinned proof and proves the Hilbert-space claim separately.

sources.title: K. Iohara, G. I. Lehrer, and R. B. Zhang, The Jones Quotients of the Temperley-Lieb Algebras, complete paper
sources.locator: Complete 22-page paper; Sections 1.2 and 2.1, PDF pp. 1-2, especially Definition 1.1, Proposition 2.1, and Remark 2.2.
sources.reading_extent: The complete 22-page PDF was inspected through the arXiv full-text view. Sections 1.2 and 2.1 define their generator/parameter convention and state the root-of-unity trace-radical boundary.

source_review.read_extent: Read the generator relations and root-of-unity idempotent statement in Sections 1.2 and 2.1.
source_review.supports: Clarifies the separate trace-radical regime referenced by the required root-of-unity page.
source_review.limitations: Their relation is f_i^2=-(q+q^{-1})f_i; that sign convention is not identified with the local positive loop parameter without an explicit conversion, and no quotient theorem is used.

source_review.read_extent: Read Proposition 2.1 and Remark 2.2 on the first root-of-unity trace degeneracy.
source_review.supports: Supports the explicit boundary that the local result makes no modular-quotient claim.
source_review.limitations: This paper is used only for context; the conditional finite projector result uses the pinned unit-denominator lemma.
